headline: Rooppur Unit 1 approved to begin nuclear reaction
summary: The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority has cleared the first reactor for criticality, paving the way for trial electricity supply by late December.
details: The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) has approved the start of a controlled chain reaction at the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Pabna’s Ishurdi.
This approval moves the unit from a static phase into active operation, opening the possibility of trial electricity supply to the national grid by late December.
BAERA Chairman Mahmudul Hasan stated that two more regulatory approvals are required before the unit can formally supply power to the grid.
The approval was previously delayed by technical complications with automatic pressure-relief safety valves, which were later resolved by a team of Russian specialists.
With first criticality, the reactor will begin its first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction, followed by a power start-up phase.
The reactor’s thermal power will initially rise to 3 percent and gradually increase to 20-30 percent before the generator is synchronised with the national grid.
Once the plant begins supplying electricity, Bangladesh will become the 33rd country in the world to generate nuclear power.
The project's original deadline was December 2025, but it has been extended to June 2028. Costs have risen to Tk 1.39 trillion due to exchange-rate changes.
caption:
Bangladesh is one step closer to becoming the 33rd country in the world to generate nuclear power.

The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) has approved the start of a controlled chain reaction at the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Pabna’s Ishurdi.

This approval moves the unit from a static phase into active operation, opening the possibility of trial electricity supply to the national grid by late December.

BAERA Chairman Mahmudul Hasan stated that two more regulatory approvals are required before the unit can formally supply power to the grid.

The approval was previously delayed by technical complications with automatic pressure-relief safety valves, which were later resolved by a team of Russian specialists.

With first criticality, the reactor will begin its first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction, followed by a power start-up phase.

The reactor’s thermal power will initially rise to 3 percent and gradually increase to 20-30 percent before the generator is synchronised with the national grid.

Once the plant begins supplying electricity, Bangladesh will become the 33rd country in the world to generate nuclear power.

The project's original deadline was December 2025, but it has been extended to June 2028. Costs have risen to Tk 1.39 trillion due to exchange-rate changes.

headline: Bangladesh signs 15-year deal with DP World to operate NCT
summary: The agreement focuses on the modernization and efficient operation of the New Container Terminal (NCT) in Chattogram, aiming to boost port and logistics infrastructure.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with a delegation led by Esa Kazim, Chairman of the Board of Directors of DP World, at the Secretariat on Thursday evening.
The discussions centered on expanding trade and investment between Bangladesh and the United Arab Emirates, focusing on the port management and logistics sector.
A key point of the meeting was the 15-year concession agreement signed between Bangladesh and DP World to operate and modernize the New Container Terminal (NCT) in Chattogram.
Under this agreement, DP World will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the container terminal and its overflow container yard.
The partnership is expected to play a critical role in increasing operational efficiency and enhancing the capacity of the country's port and logistics infrastructure.
The Prime Minister also sought further DP World investment in free trade zones and inland depots to further strengthen the economy.
caption:
A 15-year partnership with DP World is set to modernize Bangladesh's New Container Terminal.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with a delegation led by Esa Kazim, Chairman of the Board of Directors of DP World, at the Secretariat on Thursday evening.

The discussions centered on expanding trade and investment between Bangladesh and the United Arab Emirates, focusing on the port management and logistics sector.

A key point of the meeting was the 15-year concession agreement signed between Bangladesh and DP World to operate and modernize the New Container Terminal (NCT) in Chattogram.

Under this agreement, DP World will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the container terminal and its overflow container yard.

The partnership is expected to play a critical role in increasing operational efficiency and enhancing the capacity of the country's port and logistics infrastructure.

The Prime Minister also sought further DP World investment in free trade zones and inland depots to further strengthen the economy.
